questions.q: Which statement about fire/smoke dampers is most accurate?
o: They replace sprinklers in all buildings
They are specialized life-safety devices used where required to restrict fire and/or smoke movement through air-distribution openings
They are used only in plumbing stacks
They are ordinary balancing dampers only
questions.ref: Applicable Philippine fire/building regulations plus listed damper requirements; coordinate with mechanical/fire-protection design.
questions.n: Fire and smoke dampers are specialized components associated with rated assemblies and smoke-control strategies; exact requirements depend on the applicable fire/building code.

questions.q: Which space most commonly requires direct contaminant/moisture exhaust rather than relying only on recirculation?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Toilets are typical exhaust spaces because odor and moisture should be removed rather than deliberately recirculated to cleaner occupied areas.

questions.q: Which fan type is generally associated with moving air through duct systems against appreciable static pressure?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Centrifugal fans are widely used in ducted systems because they can handle useful static pressures; selection still depends on duty and system design.

questions.q: What is the primary role of a supply diffuser?
o: Introduce and distribute supply air into a space
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Diffusers deliver and spread supply air into the occupied zone while helping control throw, spread, and mixing.

questions.q: Stack effect ventilation is primarily driven by:
o: Only wind speed at roof level
Differences in air density caused by temperature and elevation
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Warm and cool air have different densities. Vertical separation between openings can create buoyancy-driven airflow, commonly called stack effect.

questions.q: Which term refers to air brought from outside the building for ventilation?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Outdoor air is air introduced from outside to dilute indoor contaminants and support ventilation.

questions.q: Why is a clear internal airflow path important in a naturally ventilated plan?
o: Air cannot effectively move between inlet and outlet openings when partitions block the path
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Openings alone are insufficient if interior partitions or closed doors obstruct the pressure-driven path through the occupied zone.

questions.q: What is make-up air?
o: A synonym for return air in every system
Air supplied to replace air removed by exhaust or process systems
Air used to inflate elevator buffers
Air trapped inside a wall cavity
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Make-up air replaces air removed by exhaust so excessive depressurization and uncontrolled infiltration are reduced.

questions.q: A 60 m³ room receives 360 m³/h of outdoor air. What is the air-change rate?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Air changes per hour equal the hourly airflow divided by room volume.

questions.q: A return-air grille is normally used to:
o: Collect room air for return to the air-handling system
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Return grilles provide an opening for room air to leave the occupied zone and enter the return-air path.

questions.q: Which system intentionally supplies and exhausts air using mechanical equipment?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: A balanced system uses both supply and exhaust fans or equivalent mechanical means so the two air streams can be deliberately controlled.

questions.q: Which air stream is taken from an occupied space and routed back toward an air-handling system?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Return air travels from the conditioned/ventilated space back toward the air-handling system and may be partly recirculated or relieved.

questions.q: Within the PRC architecture licensure syllabus, ventilation is most directly associated with which major subject area?
questions.ref: PRC Board of Architecture, Architecture Licensure Examination Syllabi — Utilities Systems coverage.
questions.n: The PRC architecture syllabus includes building utility systems within the utilities/structural/building-materials examination area.

questions.q: Which approach generally reduces ventilation fan energy when full airflow is not continuously required?
o: Demand-based or variable-speed control where appropriate
Operating every fan at full speed at all times
questions.ref: DPWH, Philippine Green Building Code User Guide (energy-efficiency provisions for mechanical systems, elevators, escalators/moving walks).
questions.n: Controls and variable-speed operation can reduce fan energy during periods of lower demand when allowed by ventilation requirements.

questions.q: A 120 m³ room requires 5 air changes per hour. What airflow rate is required?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Required hourly airflow equals the target air-change rate multiplied by the room volume.

questions.q: What is the main function of a damper in an air duct?
o: Filter all microscopic contaminants by itself
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Dampers are movable devices used to modulate, balance, isolate, or shut off airflow depending on type and application.

questions.q: A room designed to prevent contaminants from escaping into adjacent spaces is commonly maintained at:
o: Exactly atmospheric pressure with no airflow
Positive pressure relative to adjacent spaces
Negative pressure relative to adjacent spaces
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: A negative-pressure room draws air inward from adjacent spaces, helping contain contaminants within the room before exhaust.

questions.q: Exhaust air is best described as:
o: Air entering through a supply diffuser
Air used only for cooling a motor
Air permanently discharged from the building
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Exhaust air is removed from a space and discharged outdoors rather than intentionally returned to the occupied zone.

questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes ventilation from air-conditioning?
o: Ventilation is limited to natural airflow through windows
Ventilation introduces/removes air to maintain indoor air quality, while air-conditioning may also control temperature and humidity
Air-conditioning always uses outdoor air only
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Ventilation is primarily concerned with supplying, distributing, and removing air for indoor air quality. Air-conditioning may additionally control temperature, humidity, filtration, and comfort.

questions.q: Why should outdoor-air intakes be separated from exhaust outlets and pollutant sources?
o: To reduce the chance that contaminated exhaust is drawn back into the building
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Separation helps prevent short-circuiting or re-entrainment of exhaust contaminants into outdoor-air intakes.

questions.q: If average air velocity through a 0.50 m² opening is 2 m/s, what ideal volumetric airflow passes through it?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: For a uniform idealized velocity, volumetric flow is area multiplied by average velocity.

questions.q: A louver is commonly used at a building opening to:
o: Provide weather-resistant air intake or discharge while limiting direct rain entry
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Louvers are commonly used at outside-air and exhaust openings to permit airflow while helping resist rain and debris entry.

questions.q: Which space-pressure relationship is generally used when the objective is to keep contaminants from entering a clean room?
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Positive pressure causes air to tend to flow outward from the cleaner space, reducing inward migration of contaminants.

questions.q: Which design condition generally improves cross-ventilation?
o: Openings concentrated on only one interior wall
Air inlets and outlets on different sides of the space with a pressure path between them
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Cross-ventilation benefits from pressure differences and a clear airflow path between openings, commonly on different sides of a room or building.

questions.q: In a simple mechanical exhaust system, what normally causes replacement air to enter the space?
o: Air enters through intentional or incidental openings because indoor pressure becomes lower
The exhaust fan raises indoor pressure
The return duct becomes a supply duct
questions.ref: ASHRAE ventilation terminology and standard HVAC design principles.
questions.n: Mechanical exhaust removes air and typically produces slight negative pressure, drawing replacement air through openings or designated make-up air paths.
